title: Reexamine limits on White House-DOJ communications
summary: Recommends that the next administration reexamine the traditional policy restricting contact between the White House and the Department of Justice to a single channel, and consider allowing communication through additional channels.
quote: The next Administration should reexamine this policy and determine whether it might be more efficient or more appropriate for communication to occur through additional channels.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Review and reverse prior administration's litigation positions
summary: Directs the incoming White House Counsel to review all significant ongoing litigation across the executive branch, beginning during the transition, and present recommendations for reconsidering or reversing the previous administration's positions.
quote: must be prepared at the outset of the Administration to present recommendations to the President, including recommendations for reconsidering or reversing positions of the previous Administration in any significant litigation
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Reexamine press corps space at the White House
summary: Notes that media organizations have no legal entitlement to permanent workspace on the White House campus and recommends reexamining how much space the press is given there.
quote: No legal entitlement exists for the provision of permanent space for media on the White House campus, and the next Administration should reexamine the balance between media demands and space constraints
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Reconsider ties with White House Correspondents' Association
summary: Recommends that the new administration examine its relationship with the White House Correspondents' Association and consider whether a different coordinating body for the press corps would be more suitable.
quote: examine the nature of the relationship between itself and the White House Correspondents Association and consider whether an alternative coordinating body might be more suitable
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Fill 3,000 political jobs with dedicated conservatives
summary: Tasks the Office of Presidential Personnel with recruiting leaders for roughly 1,000 Senate-confirmed appointments and filling approximately 3,000 additional political positions with committed conservatives.
quote: PPO must also fill approximately 3,000 political jobs that require dedicated conservatives to support the Administration's political leadership
status_note: Broad political appointments and Schedule F conversions have proceeded government-wide, though no specific tracking of a 3,000-position target was found (Government Executive).

title: Plan political workforce needs early, including Schedule F
summary: Assigns the Office of Presidential Personnel responsibility for identifying political workforce needs early and developing plans such as Schedule F, a mechanism for reclassifying policy-influencing career positions.
quote: Identifying programmatic political workforce needs early and developing plans (for example, Schedule F).
status_note: Schedule F (rebranded Schedule Policy/Career) was reinstated via executive order on January 20, 2025, with OPM finalizing an implementing rule in 2026 (Lawfare; CRS).

title: Limit career detailees on the National Security Council
summary: Recommends keeping National Security Council staff at its reduced size of 100-150 professionals and limiting the number of career detailees from agencies to increase direct presidential control over the NSC.
quote: The next Administration should try to limit the number of detailees to ensure more direct presidential control.
status_note: The NSC staff was cut by roughly half in a May 2025 restructuring, reducing career and detailee presence and centralizing control (NPR).

title: Assign overlapping policy areas to a single council
summary: Recommends assigning policy responsibility for overlapping areas such as immigration, health care, energy, and trade to only one White House policy council to speed up policy coordination.
quote: assigning policy responsibilities to only one council where possible will help to speed up the policy-coordination process
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Launch rapid policy processes on cross-cutting priorities
summary: Calls for incoming policy councils to move quickly on cross-agency priorities the chapter lists, including countering China, enforcing immigration laws, reversing regulatory policies to promote energy production, and addressing issues of life, religious liberty, and 'wokeism' in government.
quote: incoming policy councils will need to move rapidly to lead policy processes around cross-cutting agency topics, including countering China, enforcing immigration laws, reversing regulatory policies in order to promote energy production
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Create economic opportunity working group under DPC
summary: Recommends the President establish an economic opportunity working group chaired by the Domestic Policy Council Director to coordinate development of policies promoting economic opportunity.
quote: The President should establish an economic opportunity working group, chaired by the DPC Director, to coordinate the development of policies that promote economic opportunity.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Coordinate DPC-NSC agenda on border security
summary: Recommends that the Domestic Policy Council coordinate with the National Security Council on a policy agenda to enhance border security.
quote: DPC should coordinate with the NSC on a policy agenda to enhance border security
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Put political appointees in charge of OMB apportionments
summary: Recommends selecting an OMB Director committed to restoring sign-off on apportionments of appropriated funds to political appointees (Program Associate Directors) rather than career officials, and to wielding that spending-control tool on behalf of the President's agenda.
quote: No Director should be chosen who is unwilling to restore apportionment decision-making to the PADs' personal review
status_note: OMB Director Vought has maintained political-appointee control over apportionment decisions since his February 2025 confirmation (Government Executive; CNN).

title: Split OMB resource offices to add political appointees
summary: Recommends dividing OMB's six Resource Management Offices into smaller subject-matter units, creating more politically appointed Program Associate Director positions with deputies to expand political oversight of agency policy and spending.
quote: the existing six RMOs should be divided into smaller subject-matter areas, allowing for more PADs, and each of these PADs should have a Deputy PAD
status_note: No specific reporting was found confirming a formal split of OMB's six Resource Management Offices into smaller units with additional PAD positions.

title: Reintroduce administrative PAYGO budget neutrality rule
summary: Recommends the President reintroduce administrative pay-as-you-go, a procedural requirement imposing budget neutrality on discretionary spending choices made by federal agencies.
quote: the President should reintroduce the concept of administrative pay-as-you-go, or administrative PAYGO
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Extend OIRA regulatory review to independent agencies
summary: Recommends maintaining Executive Order 12866 and requiring regulatory analysis and OIRA review of rules issued by historically independent agencies, citing an Office of Legal Counsel opinion that this is legally permissible.
quote: Regulatory analysis and OIRA review should also be required of the historically “independent” agencies as the Office of Legal Counsel has found is legally permissible.
status_note: The February 2025 'Ensuring Accountability for All Agencies' executive order requires independent agencies like the FTC, FCC, and SEC to submit significant rules to OIRA review (Government Executive).

title: Undo Biden changes to cost-benefit analysis rules
summary: Recommends the next President immediately begin undoing any Biden administration modifications to Executive Order 12866 and OMB Circular A-4, the foundations of regulatory cost-benefit analysis, and revive OIRA review of significant guidance documents.
quote: the next President should immediately begin to undo those changes and develop a rigorous, data-driven approach that will result in the least burdensome rules possible
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Reinstate Trump-era deregulatory executive orders
summary: Recommends reviving a list of Trump administration executive orders on regulation, including EO 13771 (regulatory cost caps) and EO 13777 (regulatory reform agenda), with modifications as needed.
quote: The next President should also reinstate the many executive orders signed by President Trump that were designed to make the regulatory process more just, efficient, and transparent.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Use Congressional Review Act to erase midnight rules
summary: Recommends working with Congress to maximize use of the Congressional Review Act against late-term Biden administration regulatory actions, and enacting the Midnight Rules Relief Act to allow multiple rules to be repealed in a single vote.
quote: the next President should work with Congress to maximize the utility of the Congressional Review Act (CRA), which allows Congress to undo midnight regulatory actions
status_note: Trump signed 22 Congressional Review Act joint resolutions repealing Biden-era rules as of December 2025 (Government Executive).

title: Eliminate NSC directorates not aligned with President
summary: Recommends the National Security Advisor immediately evaluate NSC staff directorates, eliminate those not aligned with the President's agenda, and replace them with new directorates to drive the President's national security priorities.
quote: the NSA should immediately evaluate and eliminate directorates that are not aligned with the President's agenda and replace them with new directorates as appropriate
status_note: NSC directorates were restructured amid the May 2025 staff cuts that reduced the council by roughly half (NPR).

title: Send nonessential NSC detailees home on day one
summary: Recommends the National Security Advisor return all nonessential agency detailees on the NSC staff to their home agencies on the first day, replacing essential detailees with staff aligned to the new President's priorities.
quote: the NSA should return all nonessential detailees to their home agencies on their first day in office
status_note: Roughly 160 NSC aides were sidelined early in the administration while staffing was reviewed for alignment with the President's agenda (NPR).

title: NSC review of all general and flag officer promotions
summary: Recommends the National Security Council rigorously review all general and flag officer promotions, prioritizing core military roles over what the chapter characterizes as social engineering and non-defense matters such as climate change and critical race theory.
quote: The NSC should rigorously review all general and flag officer promotions to prioritize the core roles and responsibilities of the military over social engineering and non-defense matters
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Merge Homeland Security Council functions into the NSC
summary: Recommends consolidating the functions of the Homeland Security Council into the National Security Council and incorporating the Office of the National Cyber Director into the NSC structure.
quote: The NSC staff will need to consolidate the functions of both the NSC and the Homeland Security Council (HSC), incorporate the recently established Office of the National Cyber Director
status_note: No specific reporting confirms a formal merger of Homeland Security Council functions into the NSC, though broader NSC restructuring occurred in 2025.

title: Reshape federal climate research program by executive order
summary: Recommends an executive order reshaping the U.S. Global Change Research Program and related climate research programs, including diverse viewpoints in assessments, and critically analyzing or refusing to accept USGCRP assessments prepared under the Biden administration.
quote: The President should also issue an executive order to reshape the U.S. Global Change Research Program (USGCRP) and related climate change research programs.
status_note: USGCRP funding was cut and NCA6's roughly 400 scientist-authors were dismissed in April 2025, though no dedicated executive order restructuring the program as specifically envisioned was identified (Columbia Climate Law; CRS).

title: Rewrite NEPA rules to streamline permitting reviews
summary: Recommends the Council on Environmental Quality rewrite its National Environmental Policy Act regulations along the lines of the 2020 reform, restoring provisions such as a ban on cumulative impact analysis and limiting the scope for judicial review.
quote: The President should instruct the CEQ to rewrite its regulations implementing NEPA along the lines of the historic 2020 effort and restoring its key provisions such as banning the use of cumulative impact analysis
status_note: CEQ rescinded its NEPA implementing regulations via an April 2025 interim final rule and finalized the change in January 2026, shifting compliance guidance to individual agencies (whitehouse.gov).

title: Abolish climate policy office; name energy coordinator
summary: Recommends an executive order abolishing the Office of Domestic Climate Policy and establishing a Senior Advisor, reporting to the Chief of Staff, to coordinate energy and environment policy across the Executive Office of the President.
quote: The President should issue an executive order establishing a Senior Advisor to coordinate the policy development and implementation of relevant energy and environment policy
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: End use of Social Cost of Carbon analysis
summary: Recommends eliminating the Interagency Working Group on the Social Cost of Carbon and ending the federal government's use of social-cost-of-carbon analysis by executive order.
quote: The President should eliminate the Interagency Working Group on the Social Cost of Carbon (SCC), which is cochaired by the OSTP, OMB, and CEA, and by executive order should end the use of SCC analysis.
status_note: Executive Order 14154 disbanded the Interagency Working Group on the Social Cost of Carbon, ending its use as federal policy (CRS).

title: Revoke EO 14020 and abolish Gender Policy Council
summary: Recommends immediately revoking Executive Order 14020 to abolish the White House Gender Policy Council and all related policies and guidance, and instead appointing a Special Assistant to the President to coordinate policies on life and family issues.
quote: The President should immediately revoke Executive Order 14020 and every policy, including subregulatory guidance documents, produced on behalf of or related to the establishment or promotion of the Gender Policy Council
status_note: Trump revoked EO 14020 and dissolved the White House Gender Policy Council on his first day in office, January 20, 2025 (whitehouse.gov).

department: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
section: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
title: End or narrow disparate-impact doctrine for civil service exams
summary: The chapter argues the legal doctrine limiting use of general-ability entrance exams (like the discontinued PACE exam) due to disparate-impact concerns should be ended by legislation or narrowed through regulation so the government can use rigorous merit-based hiring exams again.
quote: This doctrine of disparate impact could be ended legislatively or at least narrowed through the regulatory process by a future Administration.
status_note: April 2025 executive order directs agencies to end disparate-impact enforcement; regulatory follow-through ongoing.

department: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
section: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
title: Reissue Trump-era order streamlining removal of poor performers
summary: The chapter calls for reintroducing Executive Order 13839 (revoked by the Biden administration), which shortened timelines for performance improvement, expedited disciplinary action, and limited settlement agreements that alter personnel records.
quote: the order was overturned by the Biden Administration, so it will need to be reintroduced in 2025.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
section: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
title: Use pay and bonuses strategically to reward high performers
summary: Absent a comprehensive legislative overhaul of federal merit pay, the chapter recommends that political executives use existing pay authorities and fiscal awards to reward good employee performance to the extent allowed by current law.
quote: political executives should use existing pay and especially fiscal awards strategically to reward good performance to the degree allowed by law.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
section: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
title: Consolidate federal employee appeals into MSPB
summary: The chapter recommends transferring the EEOC's federal-employee discrimination section to the Merit Systems Protection Board and returning many of the Office of Special Counsel's investigatory functions to OPM, making MSPB the primary reviewer of adverse personnel actions.
quote: The EEOC's federal employee section should be transferred to the MSPB, and many of the OCS's investigatory functions should be returned to the OPM.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
section: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
title: Move federal pay toward a market-based, occupation-specific model
summary: The chapter proposes that OPM establish initial pay schedules by occupation and region, and continuously monitor turnover and applicant ratios to adjust pay, moving federal compensation closer to a market-based system rather than uniform government-wide scales.
quote: the OPM should establish an initial pay schedule for every occupation and region, monitor turnover rates and applicant-to-position ratios, and adjust pay and recruitment on that basis.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
section: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
title: Freeze top career-position hiring to block appointee "burrowing-in"
summary: The chapter recommends an immediate freeze on hiring for top career positions at the start of a new administration to prevent outgoing political appointees from converting into permanent career civil servants.
quote: What is needed at the beginning is a freeze on all top career-position hiring to prevent “burrowing-in” by outgoing political appointees.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
section: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
title: Prioritize performance, not seniority, in reduction-in-force decisions
summary: The chapter urges the President to press for reduction-in-force rules that weight employee performance above tenure and seniority when determining layoff order, reversing the current statutory ordering.
quote: A determined President should insist that performance be first and be wary of costly types of reductions-in-force.
status_note: OPM proposed rule (Mar 2026) would prioritize performance over seniority in RIFs; not yet final.

department: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
section: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
title: Eliminate duplicative government functions identified by GAO
summary: The chapter recommends identifying and eliminating functions and programs that are duplicated across Cabinet departments or spread across multiple agencies, citing GAO findings of dozens of areas of fragmentation, overlap, and duplication.
quote: A logical place to begin would be to identify and eliminate functions and programs that are duplicated across Cabinet departments or spread across multiple agencies.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
section: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
title: Reinstate Schedule F to reclassify policy-influencing career staff
summary: The chapter recommends reinstating Trump-era Executive Order 13957, which created Schedule F, allowing career civil servants in policy-influencing positions to be reclassified outside normal competitive civil service protections.
quote: It should be reinstated, but SES responsibility should come first.
status_note: Schedule Policy/Career reinstated by Day 1 executive action; final OPM rule issued Nov 2025 and applied to ~8,000 workers by June 2026. Litigation continues.

department: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
section: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
title: Reinstate Trump executive orders restricting union bargaining power
summary: The chapter calls for reinstating three Trump-era executive orders (13836, 13837, 13839) that encouraged renegotiating union contracts to favor management rights, limited paid union official time, and restricted grievance processes, all of which were revoked by the Biden administration.
quote: Executive Order 13836, encouraging agencies to renegotiate all union collective bargaining agreements to ensure consistency with the law and respect for management rights
status_note: EO 14251 excluded much of the federal workforce from collective bargaining; appeals court lifted the injunction blocking it.

department: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
section: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
title: Congress should reconsider whether public-sector unions are legitimate
summary: The chapter suggests Congress revisit the mid-20th-century bipartisan consensus that public-sector collective bargaining is incompatible with constitutional government, questioning whether such unions should be permitted in the federal government at all.
quote: Congress should also consider whether public-sector unions are appropriate in the first place.
status_note: No congressional action, but EO 14251 ended collective bargaining for ~1 million federal workers.

department: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
section: Central Personnel Agencies: Managing the Bureaucracy
title: Rapidly fill political appointee ranks from day one
summary: The chapter recommends that a new administration build a full team of political appointees from the start via close coordination between the White House Presidential Personnel Office and OPM, rather than relying on career staff and holdover appointees as happened early in the first Trump term.
quote: it would make sense to give the President direct supervision of the bureaucracy with the OPM Director available in his Cabinet.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Focus all defense planning on denying China Taiwan
summary: Recommends that all U.S. defense efforts, from force planning to posture, prioritize the ability to defeat a Chinese invasion of Taiwan before allocating resources to other missions.
quote: Require that all U.S. defense efforts, from force planning to employment and posture, focus on ensuring the ability of American forces to prevail in the pacing scenario and deny China a fait accompli against Taiwan.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Shift NATO conventional defense burden to European allies
summary: Recommends transforming NATO so that European allies field the great majority of conventional forces to deter Russia, with the United States providing primarily its nuclear deterrent and select capabilities while reducing U.S. force posture in Europe.
quote: Transform NATO so that U.S. allies are capable of fielding the great majority of the conventional forces required to deter Russia while relying on the United States primarily for our nuclear deterrent
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Expand and modernize the U.S. nuclear arsenal
summary: Recommends expanding and modernizing U.S. nuclear forces, including new theater-level capabilities, sized to deter Russia and China simultaneously.
quote: Expand and modernize the U.S. nuclear force so that it has the size, sophistication, and tailoring to deter Russia and China simultaneously.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Reform Pentagon budgeting and fast-track new technologies
summary: Recommends reforming the planning, programming, budgeting, and execution (PPBE) process, including funding mechanisms outside the traditional cycle for prototyping emerging technologies and 'Night Court' reviews to terminate underperforming programs.
quote: Develop legislation or other means of providing funding outside the traditional PPBE process for the prototyping and experimentation of emerging technologies
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Replenish munitions stockpiles depleted by Ukraine aid
summary: Recommends replenishing and maintaining U.S. stockpiles of ammunition and equipment drawn down by support to Ukraine to strengthen the defense industrial base and ensure inventory for a future conflict.
quote: Replenish and maintain U.S. stockpiles of ammunition and other equipment that have been depleted as a result of U.S. support to Ukraine.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: End informal congressional review of foreign arms sales
summary: Recommends ending the informal 'tiered review' practice under which Congress previews prospective arms transfers before formal notification, which the chapter says would cut at least 20 days from the foreign military sales process.
quote: End the tiered review process to eliminate at least 20 days from the FMS process.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Suspend MHS Genesis; require ASVAB in funded schools
summary: Recommends suspending use of the MHS Genesis electronic health record system in recruit screening and requiring all students at schools receiving federal funding to take the ASVAB military entrance exam, alongside expanded recruiter access to secondary schools.
quote: Improve recruiting by suspending the use of the recently introduced MHS Genesis system that uses private medical records of potential recruits at Military Entrance Processing Stations (MEPS)
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Expel servicemembers with gender dysphoria from military
summary: Recommends removing medical entrance exceptions for conditions such as HIV-positive status and gender dysphoria, and expelling servicemembers with gender dysphoria from military service.
quote: Exceptions for individuals who are already predisposed to require medical treatment (for example, HIV positive or suffering from gender dysphoria) should be removed, and those with gender dysphoria should be expelled from military service.
status_note: Pentagon policy directs separation processing for servicemembers with gender dysphoria, but litigation continues with mixed rulings, including an appeals court allowing enforcement pending further review (Washington Post; NPR).

title: Reinstate troops discharged over COVID vaccine refusal
summary: Recommends reinstating to active duty servicemembers discharged for declining the COVID-19 vaccine, restoring their rank, and providing back pay.
quote: Reinstate servicemembers to active duty who were discharged for not receiving the COVID vaccine, restore their appropriate rank, and provide back pay.
status_note: Trump signed an order directing reinstatement with back pay for troops discharged over COVID-19 vaccine refusal, though actual uptake has been very low (Military.com; Federal News Network).

title: Abolish Pentagon DEI offices and CRT programs
summary: Recommends eliminating critical race theory programs and abolishing the Defense Department's diversity, equity, and inclusion offices and staff, and auditing military academy course offerings.
quote: Eliminate Marxist indoctrination and divisive critical race theory programs and abolish newly established diversity, equity, and inclusion offices and staff.
status_note: A DOD task force confirmed in May 2025 that it had eliminated all DEI offices, positions, and programs across the department (war.gov; Defense One).

title: Reverse transgender military service policies
summary: Recommends reversing policies allowing transgender individuals to serve in the military and ending the use of public funds for transgender surgeries or abortion facilitation for servicemembers.
quote: Reverse policies that allow transgender individuals to serve in the military.
status_note: Transgender service policy was reversed via executive order and Pentagon directive, but implementation remains contested in ongoing litigation (Washington Post; NPR).

title: Return civilian security clearance vetting to OPM
summary: Recommends transferring responsibility for security clearance and suitability investigations of the civilian federal workforce from the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency back to the Office of Personnel Management, except for military clearances.
quote: This function should be returned to OPM except for military security clearance investigations.
status_note: The administration moved in the opposite direction from the recommendation, transferring all civilian background investigations from OPM to DOD rather than returning them to OPM (FEDmanager).

title: Grow the Army by 50,000 soldiers
summary: Recommends increasing Army force structure by 50,000 soldiers to handle two major regional contingencies simultaneously, along with budget increases and accelerated modernization programs.
quote: Increase the Army force structure by 50,000 to handle two major regional contingencies simultaneously.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Build a Navy fleet of more than 355 ships
summary: Recommends expanding the Navy to a fleet of more than 355 ships, supplemented by unmanned systems, with range and lethality as the key factors in procurement decisions.
quote: Build a fleet of more than 355 ships.
status_note: Executive Order 14269 ('Restoring America's Maritime Dominance') launched a shipbuilding revival plan in April 2025, though the Navy's current stated goal is 381 ships rather than the 355 recommended (USNI News).

title: Reestablish offensive weapons capabilities in space
summary: Recommends reversing the current defensive posture of the Space Force by reestablishing offensive space capabilities and expanding space control capability, including in cis-lunar space.
quote: Reestablish offensive capabilities to guarantee a favorable balance of forces, efficiently manage the full deterrence spectrum, and seriously complicate enemy calculations of a successful first strike against U.S. space assets.
status_note: The Golden Dome missile-defense program, including Space Force-led space-based interceptors, is underway and moves toward more active/offensive space-control capabilities (Space.com).

title: End Cyber Command role in election security efforts
summary: Recommends ending U.S. Cyber Command's participation in federal efforts to 'fortify' U.S. elections, which the chapter says creates a perception of Defense Department involvement in partisan politics.
quote: End USCYBERCOM's participation in federal efforts to “fortify” U.S. elections to eliminate the perception that DOD is engaging in partisan politics.
status_note: Hegseth ordered a halt to some Cyber Command offensive operations tied to Russia, and by 2026 the joint NSA-CYBERCOM Election Security Group reportedly had not been activated for the midterms (NBC News; CNN).

title: Pursue legislation to dismantle DHS entirely
summary: The chapter's primary recommendation is that the President pursue legislation to break up the Department of Homeland Security along mission lines rather than continue it as a single department, arguing it has never functioned cohesively since its 2003 creation.
quote: Our primary recommendation is that the President pursue legislation to dismantle the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Merge CBP, ICE, USCIS and others into new Cabinet-level border agency
summary: The chapter recommends combining Customs and Border Protection, Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Citizenship and Immigration Services, HHS's Office of Refugee Resettlement, and DOJ's immigration courts and litigation office into a single new Cabinet-level border and immigration agency of more than 100,000 employees.
quote: into a stand-alone border and immigration agency at the Cabinet level (more than 100,000 employees, making it the third largest department measured by manpower).
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Redistribute CISA, FEMA, Coast Guard, Secret Service, and TSA
summary: As part of dismantling DHS, the chapter recommends moving CISA to Transportation, FEMA to Interior or Transportation, the Coast Guard to DOJ (and DOD in wartime), splitting the Secret Service between DOJ and Treasury, and privatizing the TSA.
quote: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) be privatized.
status_note: Component restructuring reported amid DHS leadership shakeup; no completed statutory redistribution.

title: "Soft close" ineffective DHS offices pending full dismantlement
summary: Pending congressional action to dismantle DHS, the chapter recommends the Secretary use discretionary authority to shift personnel, funding, and responsibilities away from ineffective or problematic components toward mission-essential functions.
quote: the Secretary therefore can and should use his or her inherent, discretionary leadership authority to “soft close” ineffective and problematic corners of the department.
status_note: Reporting documents discretionary downsizing of DHS components; leadership turnover complicates assessment.

title: Condition FEMA grants on immigration-law and E-Verify compliance
summary: The chapter recommends requiring state and local grant applicants to certify compliance with federal immigration law, including honoring detainers, registering for and using E-Verify, and agreeing to share information with federal law enforcement, as preconditions for most FEMA grant funding.
quote: Certification by applicants that they comply with all aspects of federal immigration laws, including the honoring of all immigration detainers.
status_note: Immigration-compliance conditions attached to FEMA grants were rejected by a federal judge in Oct 2025.

title: Stop discretionary expansion of guest-worker visa authorities
summary: The chapter recommends the DHS Secretary explicitly stop using discretionary authority to raise H-2B seasonal visa numbers above the statutory cap and decline to issue regulations expanding the H-2 eligible-country list.
quote: The Secretary should make it clear that he or she will not use the Secretary's existing discretionary authority to increase the number of H-2B (seasonal non-agricultural) visas above the statutorily set cap.
status_note: No action tracked; DHS instead expanded H-2B visas above the statutory cap for FY 2026 — contrary to the recommendation.

title: Rescind ICE "sensitive zones" limits and expand expedited removal
summary: The chapter recommends rescinding all ICE memoranda that designate 'sensitive zones' where agents are prohibited from operating, and expanding use of Expedited Removal authority beyond the current practice of limiting it to aliens apprehended within 100 miles of the border.
quote: All ICE memoranda identifying “sensitive zones” where ICE personnel are prohibited from operating should be rescinded.
status_note: Sensitive-locations policy rescinded in early 2025; expedited removal expanded.

title: Fund large expansion of ICE detention capacity
summary: The chapter calls on Congress to mandate and fund a significant increase in ICE detention bed space, raising the daily available capacity to 100,000 beds, along with funding for thousands of additional enforcement officers and attorneys.
quote: ICE should be funded for a significant increase in detention space, raising the daily available number of beds to 100,000.
status_note: 2025 budget law funds major detention expansion; ICE plans to roughly double capacity by end of 2026.

title: Repeal diversity visa lottery and move to merit-based immigration
summary: The chapter recommends legislation to repeal the diversity visa lottery, end extended-family "chain migration" in favor of nuclear-family based immigration, and replace the existing employment visa system with one awarding visas based on skill.
quote: the diversity visa lottery should be repealed, chain migration should be ended while focusing on the nuclear family, and the existing employment visa program should be replaced with a system to award visas only to the “best and brightest.”
status_note: Bills to repeal the diversity visa lottery introduced in both chambers; none enacted.

title: Classify USCIS as national-security-sensitive and decertify its union
summary: The chapter recommends reclassifying all USCIS employees as holding national-security-sensitive positions with corresponding leak-investigation standards, decertifying the agency's union, and rotating D.C.-based staff out to field offices nationwide.
quote: USCIS should be classified as a national security–sensitive agency, and all of its employees should be classified as holding national security–sensitive positions.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Wind down the National Flood Insurance Program
