summary: Champions legislation repealing the federal sugar program, which restricts sugar supply to raise prices, citing consumer costs estimated at up to $3.7 billion per year.
quote: Repeal the federal sugar program. The federal government should not be in the central planning business, and the sugar program is a prime example of harmful central planning.
status_note: Rather than repealing the federal sugar program, the 2025 reconciliation law extended it by setting new loan rates through the 2031 crop year (Congress.gov, H.R.1).

title: Repeal ARC and PLC commodity subsidy programs
summary: Recommends legislation repealing the Agriculture Risk Coverage and Price Loss Coverage programs, arguing eligible farmers can already buy federally subsidized crop insurance against revenue shortfalls.
quote: Ideally, repeal the ARC and PLC programs. Farmers eligible to participate in ARC or PLC are generally already able to purchase federal crop insurance
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Cap crop insurance premium subsidies at 50 percent
summary: Proposes reducing the taxpayer share of federal crop insurance premiums, currently about 60 percent, to no more than 50 percent, citing CBO savings estimates.
quote: At a minimum, taxpayers should not pay more than 50 percent of the premium.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Split nutrition programs out of the farm bill
summary: Recommends separating agricultural provisions from food stamps and nutrition provisions in the farm bill, with reauthorizations on different timelines.
quote: agricultural programs should be considered in separate legislation distinct from food stamps and the nutrition part of the farm bill, and reauthorization of such programs should be fixed on different timelines
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Move food stamps and nutrition programs to HHS
summary: Proposes transferring USDA means-tested food and nutrition programs, including SNAP and WIC, to the Department of Health and Human Services so one department oversees all means-tested welfare.
quote: Move the USDA food and nutrition programs to the Department of Health and Human Services.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Reimpose SNAP work requirements
summary: Recommends re-implementing work requirements for able-bodied adult SNAP recipients without dependents, restricting state waivers, and clarifying state options for general work requirements.
quote: Re-implement work requirements. The statutory language covering food stamps allows states to waive work requirements that otherwise apply to work-capable individuals
status_note: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act expanded SNAP able-bodied adult work requirements effective November 1, 2025, raising the age ceiling and narrowing exemptions (USDA FNS).

title: Close SNAP broad-based categorical eligibility loophole
summary: Proposes reforming broad-based categorical eligibility, which lets states enroll individuals in food stamps based on minimal benefits from other programs, bypassing income and asset limits.
quote: Reform broad-based categorical eligibility. Federal law permits states to enroll individuals in food stamps if they receive a benefit from another program
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Reverse the Thrifty Food Plan benefit increase
summary: Calls for re-evaluating the 2021 Thrifty Food Plan update that raised SNAP benefits by at least 23 percent, which the chapter estimates added $250-300 billion in outlays over ten years.
quote: Re-evaluate the Thrifty Food Plan. In a dramatic overreach, the Biden Administration unilaterally increased food stamp benefits by at least 23 percent in October 2021.
status_note: The OBBBA bars USDA from reevaluating the Thrifty Food Plan until at least October 2027 and caps future increases to inflation, reversing the trajectory of the 2021 benefit expansion (Newsweek).

title: Restrict school meal eligibility expansion
summary: Recommends a rule barring schools from grouping to qualify for the Community Eligibility Provision, working with Congress to eliminate CEP, and rejecting universal free school meal proposals.
quote: The USDA should issue a rule that clarifies that only an individual school or a school district as a whole, not a subset of schools within a district, must meet the 40-percent criteria to be eligible for CEP.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Eliminate the Conservation Reserve Program
summary: Proposes working with Congress to eliminate the Conservation Reserve Program, which pays farmers not to farm portions of their land, in favor of targeted efforts tied to specific environmental harms.
quote: Champion the elimination of the Conservation Reserve Program. Farmers should not be paid in such a sweeping way not to farm their land.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: End commodity checkoff programs and marketing orders
summary: Recommends eliminating or reducing marketing orders and checkoff programs, described as compelled funding arrangements, and requiring regular votes by affected parties on their continuation.
quote: These programs should be eliminated, and if industry actors want to collaborate, they should do so through private means, not using the government to compel cooperation.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Expand active forest management and timber sales
summary: Recommends executive action building on Executive Order 13855 and legislation to promote vegetation management, reduce regulatory obstacles to fuel reduction in national forests, and increase timber sales.
quote: embracing Executive Order 13855, building upon it, and working with lawmakers to promote active management of vegetation, reduce regulatory obstacles to reducing fuel buildup, and increase timber sales
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Repeal or overhaul the Dietary Guidelines
summary: Recommends working with lawmakers to repeal the federal Dietary Guidelines for Americans or, at minimum, reforming the process to focus strictly on nutrition and exclude environmental considerations.
quote: Work with lawmakers to repeal the Dietary Guidelines. The USDA should help lead an effort to repeal the Dietary Guidelines.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Ultimately eliminate the federal Department of Education
summary: The chapter's stated mission is that federal education policy should be limited and the Department of Education should ultimately be eliminated, with education decisions and funding devolved to families and states.
quote: Federal education policy should be limited and, ultimately, the federal Department of Education should be eliminated.
status_note: March 2025 EO directs dismantling; mass layoffs allowed by Supreme Court; statutory elimination still requires Congress.

title: Block-grant federal education funds to states without strings
summary: The chapter recommends that federal education dollars be converted into no-strings-attached block grants to states rather than program-specific funding tied to federal rules and regulations, reducing the federal and state compliance bureaucracy.
quote: those funds should be block-granted to states without strings, eliminating the need for many federal and state bureaucrats.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Pass a Department of Education Reorganization Act
summary: The chapter recommends that the administration work with Congress to pass legislation that would reform, eliminate, or redistribute the Department of Education's programs and offices to other federal agencies as part of winding down the department.
quote: the next Administration should work with Congress to pass a Department of Education Reorganization Act to reform, eliminate, or move the department's programs and offices to appropriate agencies.
status_note: Termination bill (H.R.899) introduced; reorganization proceeding administratively rather than by statute.

title: Move Title I funding to HHS, phase out over 10 years
summary: The chapter recommends transferring Title I, Part A funding for low-income school districts to HHS as a no-strings formula block grant, and gradually shifting funding responsibility back to states over a 10-year period.
quote: Restore revenue responsibility for Title I funding to the states over a 10-year period.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Convert IDEA special-education funding into a block grant via HHS
summary: The chapter recommends converting most Individuals with Disabilities Education Act funding into a no-strings formula block grant for students with disabilities, administered by HHS's Administration for Community Living rather than the Department of Education.
quote: Most IDEA funding should be converted into a no-strings formula block grant targeted at students with disabilities and distributed directly to local education agencies by Health and Human Service's Administration for Community Living.
status_note: Special-education functions transferred out of the Education Department in June 2026.

title: Spin off federal student loans into an independent corporation
summary: The chapter recommends reversing the 2010 federalization of student lending and spinning off the Office of Federal Student Aid and its loan obligations into a new, professionally governed government corporation.
quote: The next Administration should completely reverse the student loan federalization of 2010 and work with Congress to spin off FSA and its student loan obligations to a new government corporation with professional governance and management.
status_note: Treasury–Education partnership announced to move federal student-loan servicing; independent corporation not yet created.

title: Move Office for Civil Rights enforcement to the Justice Department
summary: The chapter recommends moving the Department of Education's Office for Civil Rights to the Department of Justice, where civil rights protections would be enforced only through litigation rather than administrative agency action.
quote: OCR should move to the Department of Justice. The federal government has an essential responsibility to enforce civil rights protections, but Washington should do so through the Department of Justice and federal courts.
status_note: Office for Civil Rights enforcement functions transferred in June 2026.

title: Rescind Biden Title IX rule and restore 2020 biological-sex definition
summary: The chapter calls for rescinding the Biden administration's Title IX regulations, restoring the 2020 regulations issued under Secretary Betsy DeVos, and defining 'sex' under Title IX to mean only biological sex recognized at birth.
quote: restore the Title IX regulations promulgated by then-Secretary Betsy DeVos on May 19, 2020; and define “sex” under Title IX to mean only biological sex recognized at birth.
status_note: Biden-era Title IX rule scrapped Jan 2025; 2020 rule restored.

title: Stop Title VI school-discipline cases based only on disparate impact
summary: The chapter recommends that the Department of Education and DOJ jointly issue guidance stating they will no longer investigate Title VI school-discipline cases that rest exclusively on statistical disparate-impact allegations rather than evidence of disparate treatment.
quote: the new Administration should also direct the department and DOJ jointly to issue enforcement guidance stating that the agencies will no longer investigate Title VI cases that exclusively rest on allegations of disparate impact.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Rescind the Obama-era "Equity in IDEA" race-based regulation
summary: The chapter recommends rescinding a 2016 regulation requiring states to consider race and ethnicity when addressing disproportionality in special-education identification, placement, and discipline, arguing the underlying premise is not supported by research.
quote: The next Administration should immediately commence rulemaking to rescind the Equity in IDEA regulation. No replacement regulation is required.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Phase out existing income-driven student loan repayment plans
summary: The chapter recommends phasing out all current income-driven repayment plans for new borrowers and replacing them with a single, less generous plan requiring payments of 10 percent of income above the poverty line, with no loan forgiveness if new legislation allows.
quote: The Secretary should phase out all existing IDR plans by making new loans (including consolidation loans) ineligible and should implement a new IDR plan.
status_note: FY2025 reconciliation law replaced existing income-driven repayment plans with the Repayment Assistance Plan.

title: Rescind the National Education Association's federal charter
summary: The chapter recommends that Congress rescind the National Education Association's congressional charter, arguing the charter lends undeserved legitimacy to a union it characterizes as a partisan special interest group.
quote: Congress should rescind the National Education Association's congressional charter and remove the false impression that federal taxpayers support the political activities of this special interest group.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Pass a federal Parents' Bill of Rights with strict-scrutiny protection
summary: The chapter recommends federal legislation establishing parental rights in education as a 'top-tier' constitutional right subject to strict judicial scrutiny, giving parents a stronger legal basis to challenge federal actions affecting their children's upbringing and education.
quote: The law would require the government to satisfy “strict scrutiny”—the highest standard of judicial review—when the government infringes parental rights.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Require parental consent for schools to use different names/pronouns
summary: For K-12 systems under federal jurisdiction, the chapter proposes legislation barring school employees from addressing a student by a name or pronoun other than that on the student's birth certificate without written parental permission, and protecting staff who object on religious or moral grounds.
quote: No public education employee or contractor shall use a name to address a student other than the name listed on a student's birth certificate, without the written permission of a student's parents or guardians.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Expand and increase funding for the D.C. Opportunity Scholarship
summary: The chapter recommends that Congress expand the D.C. Opportunity Scholarship voucher program to all students regardless of income, raise the scholarship amount closer to per-pupil spending in D.C. public schools, and deregulate participating private schools' admissions and testing requirements.
quote: Congress should expand eligibility to all students, regardless of income or background, and raise the scholarship amount closer to the funding students receive in D.C. Public Schools.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Bar accreditors from mandating DEI policies at colleges
summary: The chapter recommends amending the Higher Education Act to prohibit accreditation agencies from using their gatekeeper role over federal student aid eligibility to require colleges and universities to adopt diversity, equity, and inclusion policies.
quote: Prohibit accreditation agencies from leveraging their Title IV gatekeeper role to mandate that educational institutions adopt diversity, equity, and inclusion policies.
status_note: April 2025 EO directs accreditation overhaul including DEI mandates; implementation ongoing.

title: Privatize federal student lending and end PLUS loans and PSLF
summary: The chapter recommends privatizing federal student lending programs (subsidized, unsubsidized, and PLUS loans) to introduce market-based accountability, and separately calls for eliminating Grad PLUS and Parent PLUS loans and terminating the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program.
quote: Privatizing all lending programs, including subsidized, unsubsidized, and PLUS loans (both Grad and Parent). This would allow for market prices and signals to influence educational borrowing.
status_note: Grad PLUS eliminated and loan caps enacted; new PSLF restriction rule blocked in court July 2026.

department: Department of Energy and Related Commissions
title: Repeal infrastructure and climate laws, claw back funds
summary: Supports repealing the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act and Inflation Reduction Act and rescinding all funds from those programs not already spent.
quote: Support repeal of massive spending bills like the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) and Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), which established new programs and are providing hundreds of billions of dollars in subsidies to renewable energy developers
status_note: The OBBBA repealed or accelerated the phaseout of roughly 60% of IRA clean-energy tax credits and rescinded some unobligated funds, but did not repeal the IIJA or IRA outright (CRS).

department: Department of Energy and Related Commissions
title: Rename DOE the Department of Energy Security and Advanced Science
summary: Proposes renaming and refocusing the Department of Energy around energy security, national security, fundamental science, nuclear site remediation, and nuclear weapons development.
quote: The Department of Energy should be renamed and refocused as the Department of Energy Security and Advanced Science (DESAS).
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Energy and Related Commissions
title: Eliminate DOE clean energy demonstration and loan offices
summary: Recommends eliminating or reforming the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations, Office of State and Community Energy Programs, ARPA-E, Grid Deployment Office, and DOE Loan Program.
quote: The DOE Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations (OCED); Office of State and Community Energy Programs; ARPA-E; Office of Grid Deployment (OGD); and DOE Loan Program should be eliminated or reformed.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Energy and Related Commissions
title: Fast-track LNG export approvals without climate review
summary: Calls for removing political and climate-change considerations from DOE approvals of liquefied natural gas exports and expanding automatic approvals to allies including NATO countries.
quote: Eliminate political and climate-change interference in DOE approvals of liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports.
status_note: DOE ended the Biden-era LNG export permitting pause under EO 14154 within weeks of inauguration (energy.gov).

department: Department of Energy and Related Commissions
title: Fund new nuclear warheads and plutonium pit production
summary: Recommends funding the design, development, and deployment of new nuclear warheads for each leg of the triad, including plutonium pit production at Los Alamos and Savannah River.
quote: Fund the design, development, and deployment of new nuclear warheads, including the production of plutonium pits in quantity.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Energy and Related Commissions
title: Reinstate bulk-power grid security executive order
summary: Recommends reinstating a version of Trump-era Executive Order 13920 on securing the U.S. bulk-power system, revoked in 2021, and refocusing CESER on cyber and physical infrastructure threats.
quote: A good first step would be to reinstate an iteration of the Trump Administration's Executive Order 13920, “Securing the United States Bulk-Power System.”
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Energy and Related Commissions
title: Abolish the Office of Fossil Energy and Carbon Management
summary: Proposes eliminating FECM's applied energy programs or, failing that, renaming it the Office of Fossil Energy with its original mission of increasing energy security and supply through fossil fuels.
quote: The next Administration should work with Congress to eliminate all of DOE's applied energy programs, including those in FECM (with the possible exception of those that are related to basic science for new energy technology).
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Energy and Related Commissions
title: Eliminate the renewable energy office (EERE)
summary: Recommends working with Congress to eliminate the Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy or, alternatively, sharply reducing its budget and refocusing it on fundamental research.
quote: Eliminate EERE. The next Administration should work with Congress to eliminate all of DOE's applied energy programs, including those in EERE
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Energy and Related Commissions
title: Repeal appliance energy efficiency standards
summary: Proposes modifying or repealing the law requiring energy and water efficiency standards for household and commercial appliances, and meanwhile limiting new standards under existing statutory constraints.
quote: The next Administration should work with Congress to modify or repeal the law mandating energy efficiency standards.
status_note: DOE has postponed, withdrawn, and used the CRA to roll back numerous appliance efficiency standards in 2025, though the underlying statute mandating standards has not been repealed by Congress (Utility Dive).

department: Department of Energy and Related Commissions
title: Stop new DOE loans and wind down Loan Program Office
summary: Recommends backing no new DOE loans or loan guarantees and seeking congressional sunset of DOE loan authority, eventually eliminating the Loan Programs Office.
quote: Should seek to sunset DOE's loan authority through Congress and eventually eliminate the Loan Program Office.
status_note: DOE restructured the Loan Programs Office into the Office of Energy Dominance Financing and canceled roughly $30 billion in clean-energy awards, but the office has not been formally eliminated by Congress (Latitude Media).

department: Department of Energy and Related Commissions
title: Abolish the Clean Energy Corps
summary: Calls for eliminating the Clean Energy Corps, a hiring initiative under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, by revoking funding and eliminating all associated positions and personnel.
quote: Eliminate the Clean Energy Corps by revoking funding and eliminating all positions and personnel hired under the program.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Energy and Related Commissions
title: Restart Yucca Mountain nuclear waste licensing
summary: Recommends restarting the Yucca Mountain repository licensing process, pursuing a second repository through consent-based siting, and reconstituting the Office of Civilian Radioactive Waste Management.
quote: DOE should restart the Yucca Mountain licensing process. Any continuation of interim storage facilities should be made part of an integrated waste management system that includes geologic storage.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Energy and Related Commissions
title: Reject test ban treaty and prepare for nuclear testing
summary: Recommends rejecting ratification of the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty and directing the National Nuclear Security Administration to move to immediate nuclear test readiness.
quote: Reject ratification of the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty and indicate a willingness to conduct nuclear tests in response to adversary nuclear developments if necessary.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Energy and Related Commissions
title: Require grid pricing that favors dispatchable power
summary: Proposes FERC direct regional transmission organizations to establish reliability pricing for dispatchable generation or require intermittent wind and solar resources to procure backup power.
quote: FERC should direct RTOs to establish reliability pricing for eligible dispatchable generation resources or require intermittent resources to procure backup power for times when they are not available to operate.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Energy and Related Commissions
title: Limit pipeline reviews to direct impacts, not emissions
summary: Recommends FERC confine natural gas pipeline environmental reviews to the pipeline itself, excluding indirect upstream and downstream greenhouse gas effects, and limit certificate decisions to need for the gas.
quote: Limit its NEPA analysis to the impacts of the actual pipeline itself, not indirect upstream and downstream effects.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Energy and Related Commissions
title: Speed nuclear licensing and drop ALARA radiation standard
summary: Proposes the NRC complete light-water reactor license applications within two years, expedite license extensions, and replace the ALARA radiation principle with risk- and dose-based standards.
quote: Applications for Combined Operating Licenses (COLs) and design certifications that rely on light-water technology should generally be completed within two years.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Fold enforcement office back into EPA program offices
summary: Proposes returning enforcement and compliance functions to EPA's air, water, land, and emergency management offices and eliminating the stand-alone enforcement office.
quote: eliminating the stand-alone Office of Enforcement and Compliance Assistance, which has created a mismatch between standard-setting and implementation
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Abolish EPA's stand-alone environmental justice office
summary: Recommends eliminating the stand-alone Office of Environmental Justice and External Civil Rights and returning the environmental justice function to the Administrator's office.
quote: Returning the environmental justice function to the AO, eliminating the stand-alone Office of Environmental Justice and External Civil Rights.
status_note: EPA Administrator Zeldin ordered closure of the stand-alone Office of Environmental Justice and External Civil Rights and its regional divisions in March 2025.

title: Day One executive order to reorganize and review EPA
summary: Calls for a Day One executive order requiring reconsideration of EPA's structure, with “pause and review” teams assessing major rules, pending petitions, grants, legal settlements, staffing, and budget.
quote: a Day One executive order should be drafted for the incoming President with explicit language requiring reconsideration of the agency’s structure
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Deploy vetted political appointee team on Day One
summary: Calls for the political appointee team to be assembled and vetted before Day One, with nominees serving as deputies while confirmation proceeds and appointees extended to regional offices and specialty labs.
quote: The majority of the political appointee team must be assembled, vetted, and ready to deploy before Day One.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Update the 2009 greenhouse gas endangerment finding
summary: Directs EPA to establish a system, with a deadline, to update the 2009 endangerment finding and to remove the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program for source categories not currently regulated.
quote: Establish a system, with an appropriate deadline, to update the 2009 endangerment finding.
status_note: EPA proposed repeal of the 2009 endangerment finding in August 2025 and finalized its rescission, along with vehicle GHG standards, in February 2026.

title: Limit California's vehicle emissions waiver to non-climate issues
summary: Recommends restoring the position that California's Clean Air Act waiver covers only California-specific issues such as ground-level ozone, and that other states may adopt California standards only for criteria pollutants.
quote: Restore the position that California’s waiver applies only to California-specific issues like ground-level ozone, not global climate issues.
status_note: Trump signed Congressional Review Act resolutions in June 2025 revoking California's Clean Air Act waivers, though eleven states are suing to block the rescissions.

title: Narrow the 'waters of the United States' definition
summary: Proposes a new WOTUS rule clarifying what qualifies as a navigable water and coordination with Congress to codify the Rapanos definition limiting jurisdiction to relatively permanent bodies of water.
quote: A WOTUS rule that makes clear what is and is not a “navigable water” and respects private property rights.
status_note: EPA and the Army Corps proposed a new WOTUS rule narrowing jurisdiction in November 2025; it had not been finalized as of mid-2026.

title: Revisit PFAS hazardous-substance designation under Superfund
summary: Recommends revisiting the designation of PFAS chemicals as hazardous substances under CERCLA and revising groundwater cleanup regulations for omnipresent contaminants.
quote: Revisit the designation of PFAS chemicals as “hazardous substances” under CERCLA.
status_note: EPA announced in September 2025 it will retain, not revisit, the CERCLA hazardous-substance designation for PFOA/PFOS, contrary to the recommendation to revisit it.

title: Halt EPA science work lacking congressional authorization
summary: Directs EPA to notify Congress it will not conduct science activities lacking clear congressional authorization and to include EPA quasi-regulatory actions in Inauguration Day regulatory freeze directives.
quote: Notify Congress that EPA will not conduct any ongoing or planned science activity for which there is not clear and current congressional authorization.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: End use of the social cost of carbon
summary: Recommends eliminating regulatory inputs including the social cost of carbon, proprietary models, and climate scenarios based on Representative Concentration Pathway 8.5.
quote: Eliminate the use of unauthorized regulatory inputs like the social cost of carbon, black box and proprietary models, and unrealistic climate scenarios, including those based on Representative Concentration Pathway (RCP) 8.5.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Eliminate IRIS and other unauthorized research programs
summary: Recommends eliminating several Office of Research and Development programs, citing the Integrated Risk Information System as never authorized by Congress, and rejecting funding for unauthorized science activities.
quote: Several ORD offices and programs, many of which constitute unaccountable efforts to use scientific determinations to drive regulatory, enforcement, and legal decisions, should be eliminated.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Suspend and reconstitute EPA science advisory bodies
summary: Calls for suspending and reviewing EPA advisory committees and resetting science advisory boards to change their membership composition and viewpoint balance.
quote: Suspend and review the activities of EPA advisory bodies, many of which have not been authorized by Congress or lack independence, balance, and geographic and viewpoint diversity.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Elevate and relocate the American Indian Office
summary: Proposes elevating the American Indian Office to a stand-alone Assistant Administrator office located in the American West, such as Oklahoma City, Dallas, or Denver, and consolidating all tribal grants there.
quote: AIO should be significantly elevated as a stand-alone EPA Assistant Administrator office.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Consolidate all EPA attorneys into General Counsel's office
summary: Recommends housing all attorneys authorized to represent EPA within the Office of General Counsel, moving enforcement attorneys out of OECA and disbanding the environmental justice office's legal staff.
quote: All attorneys with authority to represent EPA—not necessarily all attorneys—should therefore be housed in OGC.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Put a political appointee in charge of EPA grants
summary: Proposes a pause and review of grants over a threshold, a political appointee heading the grants office, and caps on grants awarded by the Office of Research and Development.
quote: Put a political appointee in charge of the grants office to prioritize distribution of grants to those who are most in need and toward projects that will tangibly improve the environment.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Health and Human Services
title: Split CDC into separate data and policy agencies
summary: Proposes dividing the CDC into a national epidemiological agency required to publish all collected data and a separate public health agency with severely confined policy-recommendation authority.
quote: These distinct functions should be separated into two entirely separate agencies with a firewall between them.
status_note: HHS announced a March 2025 restructuring folding several CDC functions into a new Administration for a Healthy America, but a court halted parts of the plan in July 2025 and a full CDC/policy split has not been completed.

department: Department of Health and Human Services
title: Bar CDC guidance from being prescriptive
summary: Recommends prohibiting, by statute or regulation, CDC guidance from taking on a prescriptive character, leaving decisions such as school masking or vaccination to parents, providers, and politically accountable officials.
quote: By statute or regulation, CDC guidance must be prohibited from taking on a prescriptive character.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Health and Human Services
title: Move vaccine safety monitoring from CDC to FDA
summary: Proposes transferring the CDC's vaccine safety programs, including VAERS, the Vaccine Safety Datalink, and the CISA Project, along with their funding, to the FDA.
quote: Those functions and their associated funding should be transferred to the FDA, which is responsible for post-market surveillance and evaluation of all other drugs and biological products.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Health and Human Services
title: Require states to report detailed abortion data
summary: Recommends HHS use available tools, including cutting funds, to ensure every state reports the number of abortions performed, gestational age, reason, method, and the mother's state of residence.
quote: HHS should use every available tool, including the cutting of funds, to ensure that every state reports exactly how many abortions take place within its borders
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Health and Human Services
title: Withdraw FDA approval of abortion pills
summary: Calls on the FDA to reverse its approval of mifepristone and, as an interim step, restore earlier safety protocols including in-person dispensing and an end to mail distribution.
quote: Reverse its approval of chemical abortion drugs because the politicized approval process was illegal from the start.
status_note: FDA launched a mifepristone safety review in 2026 that could lead to tighter restrictions, even as a federal court ruled in late 2025 that existing restrictions were 'arbitrary and capricious' and ordered reconsideration.

department: Department of Health and Human Services
title: End federally funded fetal tissue and embryo research
summary: Recommends restoring the ethics advisory committee for abortion-derived fetal tissue research, ending intramural NIH research using such tissue, and closing the human embryonic stem cell registry.
quote: Promptly restore the ethics advisory committee to oversee abortion-derived fetal tissue research, and Congress should prohibit such research altogether.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Health and Human Services
title: Decommission the CDC and NIH foundations
summary: Calls for decommissioning the CDC and NIH foundations, whose boards include pharmaceutical company executives, and barring private donations from influencing research funding or public health policy.
quote: The CDC and NIH Foundations, whose boards are populated with pharmaceutical company executives, need to be decommissioned.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Health and Human Services
title: Impose NIH term limits; block-grant research funding to states
summary: Proposes term limits for top NIH career leaders and congressional consideration of block-granting NIH's grants budget to states to fund their own scientific research.
quote: Term limits should be imposed on top career leaders at the NIH, and Congress should consider block granting NIH’s grants budget to states to fund their own scientific research.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Health and Human Services
title: Abolish the NIH diversity office
summary: Recommends ending the NIH practice of requiring women panelists at sponsored conferences and abolishing the NIH Office of Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion.
quote: This quota practice should be ended, and the NIH Office of Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion, which pushes such unlawful actions, should be abolished.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Health and Human Services
title: Make Medicare Advantage the default enrollment option
summary: Proposes making Medicare Advantage the default Medicare enrollment option, with a competitive bidding payment model and fewer restrictions on plan benefits and services.
quote: Make Medicare Advantage the default enrollment option.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Health and Human Services
title: Repeal Medicare drug price negotiation program
summary: Calls for repealing the Inflation Reduction Act's Medicare drug price negotiation program, characterized as government price controls, and pursuing alternative Part D reforms.
quote: This “negotiation” program should be repealed, and reforms in Part D that will have meaningful impact for seniors should be pursued.
status_note: Rather than repeal it, the administration has continued and is expanding the IRA's Medicare drug price negotiation program while narrowing its orphan-drug exclusion, contrary to the recommendation to repeal the program.

department: Department of Health and Human Services
title: Convert Medicaid financing to block grants or caps
summary: Recommends restructuring Medicaid financing through a more balanced or blended match rate, block grants, aggregate caps, or per capita caps.
quote: This system should include a more balanced or blended match rate, block grants, aggregate caps, or per capita caps.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Health and Human Services
title: Add Medicaid work requirements and benefit time limits
summary: Proposes clarifying that states may adopt work incentives for able-bodied Medicaid recipients and adding targeted time limits or lifetime caps on benefits.
quote: Add targeted time limits or lifetime caps on benefits to disincentivize permanent dependence.
status_note: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act, signed July 4, 2025, adds Medicaid work requirements for expansion populations, with state-by-state enforcement phasing in through January 2027.

department: Department of Health and Human Services
title: Cut Planned Parenthood from Medicaid funding
summary: Recommends ending taxpayer funding of Planned Parenthood and other abortion providers through Medicaid guidance and rulemaking, redirecting funds to other health centers.
quote: Policymakers should end taxpayer funding of Planned Parenthood and all other abortion providers and redirect funding to health centers that provide real health care for women.
status_note: OBBBA's one-year Medicaid defunding of Planned Parenthood was partly blocked by a district court injunction before being reinstated on appeal, then expired in July 2026 without becoming permanent.

department: Department of Health and Human Services
title: Rescind EMTALA emergency abortion guidance
summary: Calls for rescinding 2022 CMS guidance interpreting EMTALA to require hospitals to perform abortions in emergencies and ending related investigations of hospitals and physicians.
quote: HHS should rescind the guidance and end CMS and state agency investigations into cases of alleged refusals to perform abortions.
status_note: CMS formally rescinded the Biden-era guidance requiring emergency abortion care under EMTALA on May 29, 2025.

department: Department of Health and Human Services
title: Reverse redefinition of sex across HHS programs
summary: Recommends reversing, across all HHS and CMS programs, the interpretation of sex discrimination under ACA Section 1557 as covering gender identity, sexual orientation, and abortion.
quote: The redefinition of sex to cover gender identity and sexual orientation and pregnancy to cover abortion should be reversed in all HHS and CMS programs as was done under the Trump Administration.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Health and Human Services
title: Move Office of Refugee Resettlement to DHS
summary: Proposes transferring the Office of Refugee Resettlement, including duties for unaccompanied alien children, from HHS to the Department of Homeland Security and eliminating the Flores settlement agreement.
quote: The Office of Refugee Resettlement should be moved to the Department of Homeland Security.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Health and Human Services
title: Eliminate the Head Start program
summary: Recommends eliminating the Head Start preschool program and its administering office, citing safety incidents and research questioning long-term academic benefits.
quote: Given its unaddressed crisis of rampant abuse and lack of positive outcomes, this program should be eliminated along with the entire OHS.
status_note: An internal administration budget draft proposed eliminating Head Start, but the final budget sent to Congress did not include elimination; the program instead faced funding delays and withheld grants.

department: Department of Health and Human Services
title: Time-limit public health emergency declarations
summary: Proposes that Congress set a fixed time frame for public health emergencies, with the Secretary bearing the burden of proof for extensions, and codify the SUNSET rule requiring retrospective regulatory review.
quote: Congress should establish a set time frame for any PHE, placing on the Secretary the burden of proof as to why an extension of the PHE is necessary.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Health and Human Services
title: Reinstate Title X abortion separation rule
summary: Recommends rescinding the Biden administration's Title X family planning regulation and reinstating the Trump-era rule requiring strict physical and financial separation between Title X activity and abortion-related activity.
quote: HHS should rescind the Biden Administration’s regulation and reinstate the Trump Administration regulation for the program.
status_note: HHS Secretary Kennedy has said he intends to reinstate the Trump-era Title X 'Protect Life Rule' separating funding from abortion referrals, but as of mid-2026 it has not been formally reinstated, though new 2027 grant guidelines move in that direction.

department: Department of Housing and Urban Development
title: Reverse Biden-era policies department-wide at HUD
summary: Calls for a broad reversal of Biden administration policies across HUD programs and a task force of political appointees to identify and reverse actions described as advancing progressive ideology.
quote: Reset HUD. This effort should specifically include a broad reversal of the Biden Administration’s persistent implementation of corrosive progressive ideologies across the department’s programs.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Housing and Urban Development
title: Shift HUD career leadership posts to political appointees
summary: Recommends immediately assigning delegated powers to political appointees, converting current career leadership positions into political appointments, and using Senior Executive Service transfers to install aligned leadership.
quote: HUD political leadership should immediately assign all delegated powers to politically appointed PDAS, DAS, and other office leadership positions
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Housing and Urban Development
title: Add HUD Secretary to foreign investment committee
summary: Proposes an executive order making the HUD Secretary a member of the Committee on Foreign Investment in the U.S. to oversee foreign ownership of residential real estate, citing threats from China.
quote: The President should issue an executive order making the HUD Secretary a member of the Committee on Foreign Investment in the U.S.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Housing and Urban Development
title: End equity-based appraisal policies (PAVE)
summary: Recommends immediately ending the Property Appraisal and Valuation Equity (PAVE) policies and reversing related actions affecting real estate appraisal practices.
quote: Immediately end the Biden Administration’s Property Appraisal and Valuation Equity (PAVE) policies
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Housing and Urban Development
title: Cut climate initiatives and the Housing Supply Fund
summary: Recommends repealing climate change initiatives and spending in HUD's budget request and eliminating the new Housing Supply Fund.
quote: Repeal climate change initiatives and spending in the department’s budget request.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Housing and Urban Development
title: Repeal Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing rule
summary: Calls for repealing the reinstituted Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing regulation and ending other uses of special-purpose credit authorities to further equity.
quote: Repeal the Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing (AFFH) regulation reinstituted under the Biden Administration
status_note: HUD withdrew the Biden-era AFFH proposed rule in January 2025 and issued a replacement reverting to a minimal, pre-1994-style AFFH certification standard.

department: Department of Housing and Urban Development
title: Bar noncitizen mixed-status families from assisted housing
summary: Proposes recommencing a Trump-era proposed regulation prohibiting noncitizens, including all mixed-status families, from living in federally assisted housing.
quote: recommence proposed regulation put forward under the Trump Administration that would prohibit noncitizens, including all mixed-status families, from living in all federally assisted housing
status_note: HUD published a proposed rule in February 2026 to bar mixed-status immigrant families from federally assisted housing, with a public comment period running through April 2026 and no final rule yet.

department: Department of Housing and Urban Development
title: Add work requirements and term limits to housing aid
summary: Recommends reducing what it calls anti-marriage bias in housing assistance, strengthening work requirements, and implementing maximum term limits for residents in project-based and tenant-based rental assistance.
quote: Where admissible in regulatory action, HUD should implement reforms reducing the implicit anti-marriage bias in housing assistance programs
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Housing and Urban Development
title: End Housing First homelessness policies
summary: Proposes ending Housing First policies so the department addresses mental health and substance abuse issues first, shifting from permanent supportive housing toward transitional housing.
quote: end Housing First policies so that the department prioritizes mental health and substance abuse issues before jumping to permanent interventions in homelessness
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Housing and Urban Development
title: Raise FHA insurance premiums on longer mortgages
summary: Recommends increasing FHA mortgage insurance premiums for products above 20-year terms to encourage shorter-duration mortgages presented as wealth-building.
quote: FHA leadership should increase the mortgage insurance premium (MIP) for all products above 20-year terms
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Housing and Urban Development
title: Devolve HUD functions to states and other agencies
summary: Suggests Congress consider a wholesale overhaul of HUD, devolving many functions to states and localities and consolidating remaining federal functions into other agencies.
quote: Congress could consider a wholesale overhaul of HUD that contemplates devolving many HUD functions to states and localities
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Rescind Biden climate order; reinstate energy directives
summary: Calls for immediately rescinding Secretarial Order 3398 and reinstating a list of Trump-era secretarial orders on coal, offshore energy, Alaska petroleum, onshore leasing, and expedited permitting.
quote: A new Administration must immediately roll back Biden’s orders, reinstate the Trump-era Energy Dominance Agenda, rescind Secretarial Order (SO) 3398
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Resume quarterly onshore oil and gas lease sales
summary: Recommends reinstating quarterly onshore lease sales in all producing states under the model of BLM Instruction Memorandum 2018-034, with expanded public notice and comment.
quote: Reinstate quarterly onshore lease sales in all producing states according to the model of BLM’s IM 2018–034, with the slight adjustment of including expanded public notice and comment.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Maximize offshore oil and gas leasing
summary: Proposes conducting offshore lease sales to the maximum extent permitted, finalizing a new five-year plan, and working with Congress to replace five-year plans with rolling or quarterly lease sales.
quote: Conduct offshore oil and natural gas lease sales to the maximum extent permitted under the 2023–2028 lease program
status_note: BOEM released a draft 2026-2031 offshore leasing program in November 2025 proposing the most auctions in decades, but it had not been finalized as of mid-2026.

title: Restart the federal coal leasing program
summary: Recommends concluding the programmatic review of the coal leasing program and working with congressional delegations and the governors of Wyoming and Montana to restart it immediately.
quote: Conclude the programmatic review of the coal leasing program, and work with the congressional delegations and governors of Wyoming and Montana to restart the program immediately.
status_note: Interior terminated the Biden-era coal leasing environmental review in April 2025 and, under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, made about 13.1 million acres available for coal leasing.

title: Establish oil and gas leasing in ANWR Coastal Plain
summary: Calls for establishing a competitive oil and gas leasing and development program in Alaska's Coastal Plain, the Section 1002 Area adjacent to the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge.
quote: Comply with the Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act (ANILCA) and the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 to establish a competitive leasing and development program in the Coastal Plain
status_note: Interior held a court-mandated ANWR Coastal Plain lease sale in January 2025 that drew no bids; further sales were planned under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act's mandate for four sales by 2035.

title: Reinstate Trump rules on ESA, migratory birds, NEPA
summary: Recommends rescinding Biden rules and reinstating Trump rules on BLM waste prevention, Endangered Species Act critical habitat definitions, the Migratory Bird Treaty Act, and NEPA implementation.
quote: Rescind the Biden rules and reinstate the Trump rules
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Reinstate Schedule F at Interior
summary: Calls for reinstituting the Schedule F proposal on accountability in federal hiring and drawing on state agency personnel, broadening state-federal and tribal-federal cooperative agreements.
quote: President Trump’s Schedule F proposal regarding accountability in hiring must be reinstituted to bring success to these reforms.
status_note: Trump reinstated the Schedule F framework (renamed 'Schedule Policy/Career') via Executive Order 14171 on January 20, 2025, applicable across agencies including Interior.

title: Return BLM headquarters to the West
summary: Recommends relocating Bureau of Land Management headquarters and senior leadership back to the American West, reversing the Biden administration's return of headquarters positions to Washington, D.C.
quote: BLM headquarters belongs in the American West.
status_note: Legislation to relocate BLM headquarters back to Grand Junction, Colorado has been introduced in Congress, but as of mid-2026 the relocation has not been completed.

title: Put BLM police under law-enforcement-only command
summary: Recommends placing all BLM law enforcement rangers and special agents in an exclusively law enforcement chain of command, implementing a 2002 Inspector General recommendation.
quote: placing all BLM law enforcement officers (LEOs), that is, its 212 Law Enforcement Rangers and 76 Special Agents, in an exclusively law enforcement chain of command
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Let BLM dispose of excess wild horses
summary: Calls on Congress to enact laws permitting the BLM to dispose humanely of wild horses and burros, citing herd populations triple what the agency says the range can support.
quote: Congress must enact laws permitting the BLM to dispose humanely of these animals.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Revoke Alaska land orders blocking state transfers
summary: Recommends revoking Public Land Order 5150 and all other remaining decades-old BLM public land orders so Alaska and Alaska Natives can select their remaining statutory land entitlements.
quote: All other remaining BLM PLOs—all of which are more than 50 years old—should be revoked immediately.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Approve Alaska oil, gas, and mining projects
summary: Calls for approving the 2020 National Petroleum Reserve-Alaska activity plan, reinstating the 2020 ANWR environmental impact statement and lifting lease suspensions, expanding the Willow project, and approving the Ambler Road.
quote: Reinstate the 2020 Arctic National Wildlife Refuge Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) by secretarial order and lift the suspension of the leases.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Vacate the 30 by 30 conservation plan
summary: Recommends vacating Executive Order 14008's 30 by 30 plan and a Biden secretarial order that removed the requirement of state and local approval before federal land acquisitions.
quote: the new President should vacate that order, DOI under a conservative President must take immediate action on the 30 by 30 plan
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Shrink national monuments; repeal Antiquities Act
summary: Proposes a new review of national monument designations, defense of downward adjustments to obtain a Supreme Court ruling on presidential reduction authority, and repeal of the Antiquities Act of 1906.
quote: the new Administration must seek repeal of the Antiquities Act of 1906
status_note: Trump signed proclamations in July 2026 shrinking Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante national monuments by about 90%, though his legal authority to reduce (not just create) monuments remains disputed and repeal of the Antiquities Act itself has not occurred.

title: Delist grizzly bears and gray wolves under ESA
summary: Recommends delisting the grizzly bear in the Greater Yellowstone and Northern Continental Divide ecosystems, delisting the gray wolf in the lower 48 states, and ceding sage-grouse jurisdiction to western states.
quote: Delist the gray wolf in the lower 48 states in light of its full recovery under the ESA.
status_note: FWS found gray wolf listing 'no longer appropriate' and declined a recovery plan in late 2025, and grizzly bear management authority is being shifted to states, but full delisting rules for both species remained unfinalized as of mid-2026, with the grizzly rule delayed to December 2026.

title: Open tribal lands to energy and mineral development
summary: Calls for facilitating fossil fuel and mineral development on lands owned by Indians and Indian nations and restoring tribal governments' authority to enforce environmental regulation on their lands.
quote: End the war on fossil fuels and domestically available minerals and facilitate their development on lands owned by Indians and Indian nations.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Move FBI out from under the Deputy Attorney General's direct line
summary: The chapter recommends internally reorganizing DOJ so the FBI reports to the Assistant Attorneys General for the Criminal Division and National Security Division rather than directly to the Deputy Attorney General, a change described as achievable without congressional action.
quote: the next conservative Administration should direct the Attorney General to remove the FBI from the Deputy Attorney General's direct supervision within the department's organizational chart.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Review and terminate FBI investigations deemed unlawful or improper
summary: The chapter calls for an immediate, comprehensive review of all major active FBI investigations and activities upon taking office, with termination of any found to be unlawful or contrary to the national interest.
quote: Conduct an immediate, comprehensive review of all major active FBI investigations and activities and terminate any that are unlawful or contrary to the national interest.
status_note: EO 14147 ordered reviews; Jan. 6-related FBI personnel identified and senior officials fired.

title: Prohibit FBI from countering "misinformation" absent criminal nexus
summary: The chapter recommends barring the FBI from activities aimed at combating so-called misinformation or disinformation by Americans unless tied to plausible criminal activity, calling for a firewall between legitimate threat monitoring and speech policing.
quote: Prohibit the FBI from engaging, in general, in activities related to combating the spread of so-called misinformation and disinformation by Americans who are not tied to any plausible criminal activity.
status_note: EO 14147 bars federal officers from unconstitutional speech-related activity.

title: Eliminate FBI's internal General Counsel and other non-law-enforcement offices
summary: The chapter recommends eliminating FBI offices that duplicate DOJ functions, such as its roughly 300-attorney Office of General Counsel, its own Congressional Affairs office, and its own Public Affairs office, shifting those functions to the Department of Justice.
quote: Streamline the non–law enforcement functions within the FBI, such as its Office of General Counsel, and obtain those services from other offices within the department.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Seek legislation ending the FBI Director's fixed 10-year term
summary: The chapter recommends submitting a legislative proposal to Congress eliminating the statutory 10-year term for the FBI Director, aligning the position's accountability to the President with that of other agency heads.
quote: Submit a legislative proposal to Congress to eliminate the 10-year term for the Director.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Bring federal charges and sue local prosecutors who decline to enforce law
summary: The chapter directs U.S. Attorneys to bring federal charges against criminals in jurisdictions where local officials decline prosecution, and recommends legal action against local officials, including elected District Attorneys, who refuse to prosecute crimes based on political or identity-based considerations.
quote: Where warranted and proper under federal law, initiate legal action against local officials—including District Attorneys—who deny American citizens the “equal protection of the laws” by refusing to prosecute criminal offenses.
status_note: DOJ has filed suits against sanctuary states and cities; litigation ongoing.

title: Restart the DOJ's China Initiative
summary: The chapter recommends restarting the Trump-era China Initiative, a DOJ program targeting Chinese economic espionage and trade-secret theft that the Biden administration terminated in 2022.
quote: Restart the China Initiative.
status_note: DOJ revived China Initiative-style enforcement and investigations of academic researchers.

title: Review and end policies, investigations, and cases contrary to law
summary: Before the inauguration, the chapter recommends the incoming administration conduct a thorough review of all publicly available DOJ policies, investigations, and cases, and prepare a plan to promptly end any that run contrary to law or the new administration's policies.
quote: In a manner consistent with applicable law, prepare a plan to end immediately any policies, investigations, or cases that run contrary to law or Administration policies.
status_note: EO 14147 directed department-wide review of investigations and cases.

title: Argue Humphrey's Executor should be overturned
summary: The chapter recommends the DOJ formally take the litigation position that Humphrey's Executor v. United States, the precedent permitting independent agencies whose heads cannot be removed by the President at will, violates the Constitution's separation of powers.
quote: The next conservative Administration should formally take the position that Humphrey's Executor violates the Constitution's separation of powers.
status_note: Supreme Court overruled Humphrey's Executor in June 2026 (Trump v. Slaughter).

title: Direct Civil Rights Division to prosecute DEI-related discrimination
summary: The chapter recommends reorganizing DOJ's Civil Rights Division and directing it to spend its first year investigating and prosecuting state and local governments, universities, and private employers whose diversity, equity, and inclusion practices are alleged to constitute unlawful discrimination.
quote: The Civil Rights Division should spend its first year under the next Administration using the full force of federal prosecutorial resources to investigate and prosecute all state and local governments, institutions of higher education, corporations, and any other private employers.
status_note: Civil Rights Division opened DEI-related admissions and employment investigations; prosecutions pending.

title: Enforce federal law against mailing of abortion pills
summary: Citing the Dobbs decision, the chapter recommends DOJ announce its intent to enforce 18 U.S.C. sections 1461-1462, which criminalize mailing articles or drugs advertised for producing abortion, against providers and distributors of abortion pills.
quote: The Department of Justice in the next conservative Administration should therefore announce its intent to enforce federal law against providers and distributors of such pills.
status_note: No Comstock Act enforcement against abortion-pill mailing tracked as of latest reporting.

title: Move election-offense prosecutions from Civil Rights to Criminal Division
summary: The chapter recommends reassigning responsibility for prosecuting violations of 18 U.S.C. section 241 (conspiracy against rights, used for voter-fraud and ballot-related offenses) from DOJ's Civil Rights Division back to its Criminal Division.
quote: The Attorney General in the next conservative Administration should reassign responsibility for prosecuting violations of 18 U.S. Code § 241 from the Civil Rights Division to the Criminal Division where it belongs.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Overhaul DOJ grant conditions to require immigration-law compliance
summary: The chapter recommends overhauling the DOJ grant application process to include more rigorous vetting of applicants, building on the Trump-era practice of conditioning grants on compliance with federal immigration information-sharing requirements, which effectively barred 'sanctuary' jurisdictions from funding.
quote: Order an overhaul of the DOJ grant application process, to include more rigorous vetting of state, local, and private grant applicants and inclusion of more pre-application criteria.
status_note: DOJ conditioned grant funds on immigration-law compliance in Feb 2025; subject to litigation.

title: Overturn Garland-era immigration court decisions
summary: The chapter recommends the Attorney General examine and consider withdrawing or overturning every immigration decision issued by Attorney General Garland, picking up prior Trump-era immigration adjudications and reissuing related rules.
quote: Examine and consider the appropriateness of withdrawing or overturning every immigration decision rendered by Attorney General Garland.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Substantially expand political appointee ranks throughout DOJ
summary: The chapter recommends a significant expansion of political appointees across every DOJ office and component beyond typical staffing levels, with particular emphasis on the Civil Rights Division, the FBI, and the immigration courts (EOIR).
quote: The next conservative Administration must make every effort to obtain the resources to support a vast expansion of the number of appointees in every office and component across the department.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: End nonessential DOJ personnel details pending a staffing review
summary: The chapter recommends terminating and recalling all nonessential details of DOJ personnel, particularly those detailed to congressional offices, shortly after inauguration until a thorough review of departmental personnel needs is completed.
quote: the next conservative Administration should terminate and recall all details of DOJ personnel shortly after the President's inauguration.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Labor and Related Agencies
title: Ban federal funding of critical race theory training
summary: Calls for an executive order banning, and a federal law prohibiting, the use of taxpayer dollars to fund critical race theory training.
quote: Issue an executive order banning, and Congress should pass a law prohibiting the federal government from using taxpayer dollars to fund, all critical race theory training (CRT).
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Labor and Related Agencies
title: End EEO-1 racial data collection by the EEOC
summary: Proposes amending Title VII to bar the EEOC from collecting EEO-1 employment statistics by race and ethnicity, and from collecting other racial classifications in public and private workplaces.
quote: The next Administration should work with Congress to amend Title VII to prohibit the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission from collecting EEO-1 data and any other racial classifications in employment
status_note: The EEOC voted in 2026 to propose ending mandatory EEO-1 demographic data reporting; the rule is in public comment and not yet final.

department: Department of Labor and Related Agencies
title: Eliminate disparate impact as a discrimination theory
summary: Recommends that Congress eliminate disparate impact liability as a valid theory of discrimination under Title VII and other laws, so that statistical disparities alone do not imply discrimination.
quote: Eliminate disparate impact as a valid theory of discrimination for race and other bases under Title VII and other laws.
status_note: Trump signed an executive order in April 2025 directing agencies to deprioritize disparate-impact enforcement, but full elimination requires further agency and possibly congressional action.

department: Department of Labor and Related Agencies
title: Rescind EO 11246 and eliminate OFCCP
summary: Proposes that the President rescind Executive Order 11246, the 1965 order on federal contractor nondiscrimination, thereby eliminating the Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs.
quote: The President should eliminate OFCCP by simply rescinding EO 11246.
status_note: Trump rescinded Executive Order 11246 via EO 14173 in January 2025, and DOL proposed formally rescinding its implementing regulations in July 2025, eliminating OFCCP's core enforcement authority.

department: Department of Labor and Related Agencies
title: Limit Bostock; rescind gender identity regulations
summary: Recommends confining the Bostock decision's sex-discrimination protections to hiring and firing, withdrawing agency guidance applying it more broadly, and rescinding regulations covering sexual orientation and gender identity.
quote: The new Administration should restrict Bostock’s application of sex discrimination protections to sexual orientation and transgender status in the context of hiring and firing.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Labor and Related Agencies
title: Require time-and-a-half pay for Sabbath work
summary: Proposes amending the Fair Labor Standards Act so workers are paid time and a half for hours worked on the Sabbath, defaulting to Sunday, with exemptions for religious observers of other days and certain employers.
quote: require that workers be paid time and a half for hours worked on the Sabbath
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Labor and Related Agencies
title: Restore Trump-era independent contractor rules
summary: Calls for the NLRB and DOL to return to their 2019 and 2021 rules defining who qualifies as an independent contractor, and for Congress to set a bright-line control-based test across federal laws.
quote: NLRB and DOL should return to their 2019 and 2021 independent contractor rules that provided much-needed clarity for workers and employers.
status_note: DOL proposed rescinding the 2024 independent-contractor rule in February 2026 and returning to the Trump-era 'economic reality test'; the rule remained in public comment as of mid-2026.

department: Department of Labor and Related Agencies
title: Narrow the joint employer standard to direct control
summary: Recommends that DOL and the NLRB define joint employment based on direct and immediate control, and that Congress codify that standard through the Save Local Business Act.
quote: DOL and NLRB should return to the long-standing approach to defining joint employers based on direct and immediate control.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Labor and Related Agencies
title: Recreate industry-recognized apprenticeships by statute
summary: Proposes that Congress expand apprenticeships outside the Registered Apprenticeship Program by recreating the Industry-Recognized Apprenticeship Program in statute, with trade associations, schools, and religious organizations able to oversee programs.
quote: Congress should expand apprenticeship programs outside of the RAP model, re-creating the IRAP system by statute
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Labor and Related Agencies
title: Open hazardous jobs to teens with parental consent
summary: Recommends that DOL amend its hazard-order regulations so teenage workers can work in currently restricted dangerous occupations with proper training and parental consent.
quote: DOL should amend its hazard-order regulations to permit teenage workers access to work in regulated jobs with proper training and parental consent.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Labor and Related Agencies
title: Require secret ballots for union recognition
summary: Proposes that Congress end card-check union recognition and require that unions be recognized only through secret-ballot elections.
quote: Congress should discard “card check” as the basis of union recognition and mandate the secret ballot exclusively.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Labor and Related Agencies
title: Bar ESG investing in worker retirement plans
summary: Calls for DOL to prohibit ERISA retirement plan fiduciaries from investing based on environmental, social, and governance factors unrelated to investor risk and return, returning to a pecuniary-factors-only approach.
quote: DOL should prohibit investing in ERISA plans on the basis of any factors that are unrelated to investor risks and returns.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Labor and Related Agencies
title: Prohibit Thrift Savings Plan investments in China
summary: Recommends that DOL use its oversight of the Federal Retirement Thrift Investment Board to bar the federal Thrift Savings Plan from investing in China, and that Congress enact a statutory prohibition.
quote: DOL should exercise its oversight of the FRTIB to prohibit investments in China.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Labor and Related Agencies
title: Cap and phase down H-2A farm worker visas
summary: Proposes that Congress cap the H-2A agricultural guest worker visa program at current levels and phase it down over 10 to 20 years; a similar cap and phasedown is urged for H-2B visas.
quote: Congress should immediately cap this program at its current levels and establish a schedule for its gradual and predictable phasedown
status_note: Congress has not capped or phased down the H-2A program as recommended; usage instead grew to nearly 400,000 workers in 2025, contrary to the recommendation.

department: Department of Labor and Related Agencies
title: Require 70 percent U.S.-citizen staffing on federal contracts
summary: Recommends that Congress require new federal contractors to employ at least 70 percent U.S. citizens, rising to at least 95 percent over ten years, and legalize employer preferences for hiring citizens.
quote: Congress should mandate that all new federal contracts require at least 70 percent of the contractor’s employees to be U.S. citizens, with the percentage increasing to at least 95 percent over a 10-year period.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

department: Department of Labor and Related Agencies
title: Maximize political appointees; replace agency counsels Day One
summary: Calls for maximizing the number of political appointees at DOL, imposing a career hiring freeze, and installing new EEOC and NLRB general counsels on Day One despite their term appointments.
quote: The number of political appointees should be maximized in order to improve the political accountability of the department.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Abolish DOT discretionary grants; shift to state formulas
