quote: Of course, the consumer welfare standard must guide FTC action, but, in appropriate situations and with strong evidence, this standard must be expanded to include more factors than just price.
status_note: FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson made Big Tech antitrust enforcement a stated priority and pressed forward with litigation seeking to break up Meta.

title: Examine government's own role in market concentration
summary: Recommends the FTC consider how regulation and regulatory capture sustain market concentration in industries including pharmaceuticals, healthcare, avionics, banking, and real estate brokerage.
quote: The FTC must consider, therefore, the role of government itself in maintaining market concentration in areas ranging from pharmaceuticals and healthcare to avionics, banking, and real estate brokerage.
status_note: No correlated reporting tracked yet; status defaults to Proposed.

title: Revisit FTC independence and Humphrey's Executor
summary: Presents the view that the FTC's structure of commissioners not removable at will may violate Article II, that Humphrey's Executor is ripe for revisiting, and that some conservatives would move antitrust enforcement solely to the DOJ.
quote: conservatives have long believed in either ending law enforcement activities of independent agencies or ending their independent status

title: Create ESG/DEI collusion task force
summary: Recommends the FTC establish a task force to investigate whether firms, particularly in private equity, use ESG or DEI practices as a means to meet targets, fix prices, or reduce output.
quote: The FTC should set up an ESG/DEI collusion task force to investigate firms—particularly in private equity—to see if they are using the practice as a means to meet targets, fix prices, or reduce output.

title: Congressional probe of ESG as anticompetitive cover
summary: Calls on Congress to investigate whether ESG practices serve as cover for anticompetitive activity or unfair trade practices.
quote: Congress should investigate ESG practices as a cover for anticompetitive activity and possible unfair trade practices.

title: Treat politically motivated service denials as unfair practices
summary: Argues that businesses refusing service based on customers' political or social views can commit an unfair trade practice when they are publicly traded, highly regulated, legally privileged, hold market power, and pursue a political agenda.
quote: This type of behavior can rise to the level of an unfair trade practice when the business is (1) publicly traded; (2) highly regulated; (3) enjoys legal privileges; (4) enjoys market power

title: Scrutinize platform advertising and contracts with children
summary: Recommends the FTC examine internet platforms' advertising to and contract-making with children as a deceptive or unfair trade practice, possibly requiring written parental consent.
quote: The FTC should examine platforms’ advertising and contract-making with children as a deceptive or unfair trade practice, perhaps requiring written parental consent.

title: Bring cases over child contracts lacking parental consent
summary: Recommends the FTC institute unfair trade practices proceedings against entities that enter into contracts with children without parental consent; the chapter notes some conservatives prefer an educational role instead.
quote: The FTC can and should institute unfair trade practices proceedings against entities that enter into contracts with children without parental consent.

title: Formalize FTC cooperation with state attorneys general
summary: Recommends creating a dedicated role in the FTC Chairman's office for state attorney general cooperation and convening state AGs to discuss enforcement in sectors such as Big Tech and hospital and supermarket mergers.
quote: establishing a distinct role in the FTC Chairman’s office focused on state AG cooperation and inviting state AGs to Washington, D.C., to discuss enforcement policy in key sectors under the FTC’s jurisdiction

title: Return authority to FTC regional offices
summary: Recommends the FTC consider restoring authority to its regional offices, whose reach has shrunk over recent decades; the chapter notes other conservatives oppose expanding regional offices.
quote: The FTC should consider returning authority to these offices.

title: Take more proactive antitrust approach to Big Tech
summary: Argues that because inaction can injure institutions such as democratic accountability and free speech, a more proactive antitrust enforcement approach toward dominant internet platforms may be warranted.
quote: failing to take antitrust enforcement action (Type I error) includes the possibility of real injury to the structure of important American institutions such as democratic accountability and free speech
status_note: The FTC under Ferguson continued pursuing antitrust action against dominant internet platforms, including the Meta breakup case, reflecting a more proactive enforcement posture.

title: Refine consumer-surplus measurement and behavioral analysis
summary: Recommends the FTC become more sophisticated in measuring consumer surplus and consider behavioral explanations, such as habit, for how platforms create and keep market power.
quote: The FTC must become more sophisticated in measuring consumer surplus. In addition, the FTC should be open to behavioral explanations, such as habit and small hedonic differences, as keys to how platforms create and keep market power.
